newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's banks to cut rates by one percentage point.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's banks to cut rates by one percentage point.

text.p: Algeria's banks will cut interest rates by one percentage point starting July 1, the country's bankers' association said on Tuesday in a statement quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS.
The cut, the fourth in the past 18 months, will bring interest rates down to a 14 percent-18.5 percent range beginning on July 1 from the current 15 percent-19.5 percent levels, the statement said.

The rate drop came as results of falling inflation and of the key rediscount rate, according to the Financial Institutions and Banks Professionals Association, which groups almost all Algeria's bankers.
The prime rate, the borrowing rate charged by Algerian banks to their best clients, stands at 15 percent allowing the interest rate to swing between 15 percent and 19.5 percent.
The Algerian government has forecast inflation will plunge to about nine percent in 1997 compared to 18 percent in 1996 and 29.8 percent in 1995, officials say.
